challenges.challenge: Maybe Supabase sanitizes signup metadata, or the app never reads the flag from public.users?
challenges.recheck: Supabase signUp options.data maps directly to raw_user_meta_data (client-controlled, documented behavior). auth.ts:33 computes isPlatformAdmin from dbUser.is_platform_admin OR ADMIN_EMAILS. public.users row is written by the trigger with the tainted flag. Neither layer sanitizes. ADMIN_EMAILS fallback does not remove the db-flag path.

challenges.challenge: Including blank cards may be intentional so merchants can self-assign purchased hardware; maybe PATCH is still blocked elsewhere?
challenges.recheck: Blank cards have no ownership column; there is no per-org claim mechanism. PATCH /api/cards/[id] authz is getCardById(id, org.id) which uses the same !c.location_id inclusion, then updateCard has no org constraint. No other gate. Intent or not, every org can read and claim every blank card across the platform.

challenges.challenge: Maybe platform admins are expected to have a personal org only and assignment to merchants happens out-of-band?
challenges.recheck: Page copy: 'assign to merchants on-site'; modal title 'Assign Hardware'; PRD operator flow expects cross-org assignment. /api/admin/assign accepts any location_id (no org check), but the UI dropdown only ever contains admin-org locations, so the workflow is unreachable in practice. getAllInventoryCards dead code confirms the intended data source was never wired.

challenges.challenge: Maybe yesterday is accumulated via c.stats elsewhere?
challenges.recheck: CardWithStats.stats has no yesterday field (types.ts:111-123); forEach in getAnalyticsOverview (db.ts:584-591) never touches yesterday. Expression reduces to round(today/1*100).

challenges.challenge: Maybe Next.js normalizes the query param name?
challenges.recheck: searchParams.get('locationId') is exact-match; caller sends location_id. No normalization. Filter silently undefined.

challenges.challenge: router.push() with external URL may be ignored by Next router?
challenges.recheck: App Router router.push with an absolute http(s) URL performs a full-window navigation (documented; same as Link href). No same-origin check is applied to the string. The middleware variant is safe (url.pathname assignment) but the client-side post-login push is not.

challenges.challenge: Hosted Supabase applies platform-level auth rate limits already; is the finding overstated?
challenges.recheck: True: hosted Supabase throttles auth endpoints by default (per-IP). That mitigates login/signup brute force partially (configurable, off by default in some tiers / self-hosted). Card creation (POST /api/cards) has no platform-level or app-level limit at all. PRD SR-006 explicitly requires app-side basic limits. Finding stands with mitigation noted; severity stays medium.
challenges.note: Scope reduced: auth endpoints partially covered by Supabase defaults; card-creation limit fully absent.

challenges.challenge: Are the buckets actually inconsistent in the real deployment target?
challenges.recheck: Vercel Node runtime runs in UTC, so server-local midnight == UTC midnight == chart bucketing. Discrepancy appears only on non-UTC hosts (self-host, some containers) or local dev. Not a defect on the documented deployment target.
challenges.note: Referee should dismiss for the intended deployment; keep as a hardening note.

challenges.challenge: Public SELECT policies may be required for the /q,/n redirect flow; and can anon REST really read everything?
challenges.recheck: Redirect routes use getAdminClient (service role) which bypasses RLS entirely - the public policies are not needed by any code path (grep: no anon/browser client reads cards/locations). Anon-key REST reads are unauthenticated by design; with USING(true) the full tables are enumerable. Public INSERT on interactions likewise unused (recordInteraction uses admin client) but allows arbitrary row injection via REST.
challenges.note: Severity raised: includes unrestricted interaction INSERT, not just SELECT.

challenges.challenge: Is window.location.origin not equally 'wrong' on preview URLs?
challenges.recheck: Preview shows what you are currently looking at (self-consistent); print page hardcodes a possibly-unrelated domain. The two disagree exactly when NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is unset and host != reviewtap.id. Printed QR is permanent media - failure mode is expensive.

challenges.challenge: Is this a bug today at pilot scale?
challenges.recheck: No incorrect behavior at current scale; it is an unbounded-growth design risk. Should be architectural/manual-review, not an autofix.

challenges.challenge: err.message leak - does Supabase actually expose schema details?
challenges.recheck: Postgres errors via supabase-js include constraint/relation text (e.g. duplicate key value violates unique constraint "cards_inventory_code_key"). Confirmed pattern across 7 handlers.

challenges.challenge: Is client-chosen inventory_code actually harmful given uniqueness constraint?
challenges.recheck: Uniqueness prevents duplicates but not format abuse, cross-range squatting (RT- prefix poisoning of batch counter), or error-500 UX. replaceCard dead-code risk noted. Medium-low at worst; keep as validation finding.
challenges.note: Severity: medium (affects operator batch pipeline integrity).

notChallengedReason: Directly re-verified by grep/read during Hunter pass (param names, dead code, empty onClick, race window, unrendered error param); evidence is mechanical.
